words.why: Here portatelo is porta + te + lo, a command to one person to take the coat with them. hai confirms singular tu.

words.form: form of avere used with tu

l136-6.text: Prendi il libro e portatelo a casa.

words.form: tu form of prendere; also the tu command: take
singular porta + te + lo: take it with you; plural portate + lo: you all bring it
words.why: portatelo here is singular porta + te + lo: take the book with you. prendi also addresses one person.

l136-7.text: Il cappotto è qui: portatelo voi, per favore.

words.form: form of essere used with lui, lei, Lei or a thing
singular porta + te + lo: take it with you; plural portate + lo: you all bring it
words.why: Here portatelo is plural portate + lo, with just one attached pronoun. voi explicitly means you all.

l136-8.text: Portate la giacca e il cappotto.

words.form: second-person plural present or voi command of portare: you all bring or take
words.why: portate addresses two or more people: bring, all of you.

words.form: the, for a feminine word

l136-9.text: Hai freddo? Te lo porto subito, il cappotto.

words.form: form of avere used with tu

words.why: te lo means it to you. The masculine object is then named at the end: il cappotto.

words.form: present form of portare used with io

l136-10.text: Questo libro è pesante: puoi portarlo tu?

words.form: form of essere used with lui, lei, Lei or a thing
form of potere used with tu
portare drops final e before lo: carry, bring or take him or a masculine thing
words.why: portarlo is portare without its final e, plus lo for libro.
tu emphasizes who should carry the heavy book.

l137-1.text: Hai voglia di venire da me dopo?

words.form: form of avere used with tu

words.why: avere voglia di means feel like or want to do something. Here di introduces venire.
da me means to my place here, with the verb venire.

words.form: stressed form of io; also mi becomes me before lo, la, li, le or ne

l137-2.text: Non ho voglia di ridere adesso.

words.form: form of avere used with io

words.why: non avere voglia di + infinitive means not feel like doing something.

l137-3.text: Hai voglia di un caffè o di un tè?

words.form: form of avere used with tu

words.why: di introduces the thing desired, a coffee or tea, in avere voglia di.

words.form: masculine singular: a or an before a noun; also one before a masculine noun
masculine singular: a or an before a noun; also one before a masculine noun
first-person singular present of preferire: I prefer
words.why: preferire takes a following infinitive directly: preferisco restare, I prefer to stay.

words.form: second-person singular present of preferire: you prefer
words.why: preferisci addresses one person as tu. The following mangiare stays infinitive.

words.form: second-person singular present of ridere: you laugh; also the affirmative tu command

l137-7.text: Ho già mangiato, preferisco un caffè.

words.form: form of avere used with io
past participle of mangiare, used here with avere
first-person singular present of preferire: I prefer
masculine singular: a or an before a noun; also one before a masculine noun
short pronoun: me, to me, or reflexive myself, depending on the construction
form of piacere used with one liked thing or an activity

l137-9.text: Preferisci un film o una passeggiata?

words.form: second-person singular present of preferire: you prefer
masculine singular: a or an before a noun; also one before a masculine noun
feminine singular form: a or an before a noun, or one when standing alone

l137-10.text: Hai voglia di una passeggiata dopo il film?

words.form: form of avere used with tu

words.why: di introduces the desired activity as a noun, una passeggiata.

words.form: feminine singular form: a or an before a noun, or one when standing alone
